text:
### Observed differences

- The traces divide into two mutually exclusive branches. In the earlier window, about 45 in 100 traces contain A01, A06 and A08 — these three always occur together and never without one another — while the remaining about 55 in 100 contain A03, A04, A11 and A12, likewise always together. No trace mixes the groups: A01 and A03, for example, never co-occur, and every trace contains exactly one of the two. [REL002, REL005, REL007, REL022, REL029, REL037]

- In the later window the take-up of these branches shifted by about 8 in 100 traces: the A01/A06/A08 branch appears in about 53 in 100 traces (90 of 200 before, 106 after) and the A03/A04/A11/A12 branch in about 47 (down from 55). The pairwise relations show the same move with the branches still never overlapping (A01-only traces 45%→53%, against A03/A04/A11/A12-only traces 55%→47%), and the differences are larger than in about 85–90 in 100 comparable random re-splits of the pooled data. [OCC001, OCC003, OCC006, OCC008, OCC011, OCC012, REL002, REL010, REL024, REL050]

- The pattern fits a re-weighting of existing paths rather than an added, removed or bypassed one: every branch member keeps a substantial share in both windows (core members about 45–55 in 100, the optional A07 and A10 about 25–27), and the lower mean occurrences of A03 and A12 (about 1.2→1.0 per trace) simply track their lower participation, with repeats per containing trace roughly stable at about 2.2→2.1. [OCC001, OCC003, OCC004, OCC007, OCC010, OCC011, OCC012]

- The optional members stay tied to their branches: A07 occurs only inside A01 traces (about 26→25 in 100, essentially unchanged) and A10 only inside A03 traces (about 27→25 in 100). [OCC007, OCC010, REL006, REL009, REL025, REL028]

- A second, embedded alternative also moved: A02 and the pair A05+A09 are strict alternatives — never in the same trace, with every trace containing exactly one — and in the later window A05+A09 (always executed in the order A05 before A09) rises from about 46 to about 52 in 100 traces while A02 falls from about 55 to 48. [OCC002, OCC005, OCC009, REL014, REL018, REL042]

- Two smaller differences: within the growing branch, A06's outgoing transitions shifted from A07 (about 53%→41% of A06's outgoing transitions) toward A08 (44%→53%), with a rare transition to A09 appearing (about 4%); and A07 and A10 repeated less often per trace (mean occurrences about 0.52→0.41 and 0.66→0.52) although their participation stayed near 25 in 100. [DIR006, OCC007, OCC010]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the two windows differ in how often two existing, mutually exclusive branches are taken: the branch built around A01, A06 and A08 (with optional A07) ran in about 53 in 100 later-window cases versus about 45 in 100 earlier, while the complementary branch built around A03, A04, A11 and A12 (with optional A10) fell from about 55 to about 47 in 100. The support is direct and consistent: an identical shift of about 8 in 100 traces appears in the participation of every core member and in the pairwise relations that establish the branches never share a trace, while all involved activities remain well observed in both windows, the branches' internal order and repetition are essentially unchanged, and no activity drops out or becomes near-universal — the picture of existing alternative paths being taken with different frequencies rather than of activities added, removed or bypassed. [OCC001, OCC003, OCC004, OCC006, OCC008, OCC011, OCC012, REL002, REL005, REL022, REL024]

The main competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is sampling variation between the two finite windows: the evidence carries no screening baseline against which the number of flagged items could be compared with what an unchanged process would produce, and although the key differences are coordinated in direction across all branch members, individually they are larger than roughly 85–90 in 100 random re-splits rather than extreme. The evidence also shows only that the take-up shifted, not what produced the shift. [OCC001, REL002]

Other differences: The choice between A02 and the A05→A09 pair moved toward A05+A09 (about 46→52 in 100 traces), mainly through gains inside the A01 branch — A05's co-occurrence with A01 rose from about 20 to 28 in 100 while its co-occurrence with A03 stayed near 25 in 100 — so it may largely be a consequence of the same mix change; A06's successor mix within its branch shifted from A07 toward A08 and A09; and A07 and A10 show fewer repeats per trace. These are not part of the branch-take-up hypothesis above. [DIR006, OCC007, OCC010, REL004, REL023]
